title: Interface guardrails for versioned models: formats, signals, and published performance profiles
creator: Ava Martinez
description:
Problem: Customers pin model versions and expect stable prompt/response behavior and predictable performance. We lack a standardized, machine-readable artifact and policy that defines what can change across model uploads and what requires a new pinned-version publication. This ticket defines the interface guardrails — (1) prompt/input format guarantees, (2) output shape/metadata expectations, (3) decoding/parameter semantic stability, and (4) the canonical published performance profile format and publication rules.

Goal: Produce a spec + onboarding checklist + small reference implementation that model owners and runtime can use to ensure backward compatible uploads for pinned versions and to publish a performance profile that Console/SDKs can consume for routing, cost estimates, and SLOs.
acceptance_criteria:
1) A spec document (YAML/JSON schema) describing required fields for a 'pinned-model manifest' that includes: schema_version, model_id, pinned_tag, incompatible_changes, stable_parameters, expected_output_shape, canonical_inputs (seed prompts), and performance_profile.
2) A published policy that enumerates allowed non-breaking changes and what constitutes a breaking change (requires notifying customers and bumping pinned_tag).
3) A lightweight reference validator (node/python) that takes a model artifact + manifest and returns pass/fail + human-readable diff.
4) Console integration: Console reads performance_profile fields and surfaces latency R95, token cost estimate, and memory footprint.
5) Integration tests that run against two sample model uploads showing accepted patch and rejected breaking change.
6) Documentation page + onboarding checklist for model owners.
technical_decisions:
1) Manifest format: primary canonical artifact will be JSON-LD with a minimal YAML-friendly alias. Use 'schema_version' to allow evolution.
2) Stability levels: REQUIRED_STABLE (no change allowed), TOLERATED_VARIATION (may vary within tolerances), ADVISORY (may change, caller warned). Map these to decoder/parameter fields.
3) Output shape description uses a small DSL: {sequence, tokens, choices, tooling} plus optional JSON schema for structured outputs.
4) Performance profile fields: r50_latency_ms, r95_latency_ms, tokens_per_second, gpu_vram_peak_mb, cpu_vram_mb, cost_estimate_per_1k_tokens_usd.
5) Backward-compatibility policy: any change to REQUIRED_STABLE fields or output JSON schema evolution that removes fields is breaking. Non-breaking changes require adding 'compatible_with' hints.
6) Validator: run static checks + a lightweight dynamic check that runs 10 representative prompts to validate output shape and latency bounds.
7) Publication: model owners must include attestations: 'tested_with_validator_v', 'published_date', optional 'regression_eval_link'.

Rationale: JSON-LD allows linking and future metadata while remaining easy to parse. Having explicit stability levels avoids ad-hoc decisions during uploads and gives customers clear guarantees.
rollout_plan:
Phase 1 (this ticket): spec + validator + docs + sample models. Phase 2: Console read/display only (no hard enforcement) for two months to gather feedback. Phase 3: Enforce validator during private model upload for new pinned versions and surface warnings for existing pins. Phase 4: SDKs will expose 'is_compatible_with' helper and recommend defaults for routing.

Milestones:
- Week 1: Draft spec + sample JSON manifests.
- Week 2: Validator prototype + unit tests.
- Week 3: Console UI read-only integration + docs.
- Week 4: Integration tests and release notes.

Rollback: If validator causes widespread rejections, revert to Console-only mode and provide a 'migration-assist' tool.
qa_testing:
- Unit tests for schema validator (coverage > 90%).
- Integration tests: two sample model bundles: one with a permissible change (e.g., improved tokenization details) and one with breaking change (removed output field). Validator must accept first and reject second.
- Performance smoke: run 10 prompts from canonical_inputs against CI runtime to verify r95 within 20% of declared r95.
- End-to-end: upload flow in staging with Console showing performance_profile and compatibility flags.
- Usability: PM + Design review of Console wording for compatibility and impact messages.
